Personality: Roman Mstislavich was the father of Daniil and Vasylko and ruled Volhynia and Galicia. In 1199 he united princely power over the two lands. He was killed near Zawichost in 1205 during warfare with Polish forces. His standing and inheritance gave his sons a foundation for seeking power while leaving political support that had to be rebuilt. The family remembers the establishment and succession of his rule and the political obligations he left behind.
